summary: This sermon explores fasting as a spiritual discipline that amplifies prayer by helping believers hear God more clearly and positioning them to be heard by God. The speaker emphasizes that fasting is not a religious obligation to manipulate God but a practice that quiets the flesh, increases spiritual alertness, and fosters deeper union with God.
key_points: Fasting and prayer are consistently paired throughout Scripture
Fasting modifies us, not God—it puts our body and soul in a posture of alertness and humility
Fasting helps us hear God's voice by denying our most basic fleshly need
The goal of prayer and fasting is not to get what we want from God but to get God himself—union with the Trinity
Physical benefits of fasting (increased blood flow, neuroplasticity, mental clarity) support spiritual receptivity
big_idea: Fasting amplifies prayer not by pressuring God to respond, but by quieting our flesh and aligning our whole selves—body, mind, and spirit—to hear God's voice more clearly and enter into deeper communion with Him.
title: FASTING: To Amplify Our Prayers
